parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, and the 2025 high-court ruling ended criminal exposure for private consensual conduct, leaving the conduct provisions exempting such acts. Rule of law functions: courts strike down unconstitutional law, and the 2022 domestic-violence act is in force with gender-neutral definitions, an explicit bar on discrimination by public officers and service providers on grounds including gender identity, and equal access for trans victims to protection orders — a traveller-facing paper protection, backed by documented police/ports/customs/prison sensitisation (dated mid-2010s). No documented trans-specific targeting, police extortion, facility ban, custody rule or service-refusal pattern exists; the only violence record is two dated, denominator-free incidents against gay men (2011, 2019), too weak to establish a rate, though anti-gay slurs and the country's UN SOGI-declaration opposition signal real social conservatism. Open questions (facilities, entry documents, custody, ward placement) are not proven exposures. Lacking direct evidence of acceptance or demonstrated enforcement for trans visitors, it sits a step below the acceptance-with-working-protections tier.
